question: Why do nurses need to know emergency devices very well before a crisis happens?

options.A: To prevent equipment theft in the ward
options.B: To ensure fast and effective action during high-stress moments
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To avoid having to document patient care tasks

explanation: Spot on! In an emergency, knowing your tools right away helps you act fast and save precious time. You are doing great! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h1)

question: Which of these is a well-known risk factor for developing preeclampsia?

options.A: Eating a high-protein diet
options.B: Carrying a fourth or fifth child
options.C: Being younger than 20 years old
options.D: First-time pregnancy (nulliparity)

explanation: First-time mums' bodies are experiencing pregnancy for the very first time, which statistically gives them a higher chance of developing preeclampsia.

question: What is the biggest danger of constant, severe scratching when a patient has a skin rash?

options.A: Triggering sudden total hair loss across the entire scalp
options.B: Permanently altering the chemical balance of natural sweat glands
options.C: Breaking the skin barrier through scratching and introducing bacterial infections
options.D: Causing the patient's blood pressure to drop rapidly into shock

explanation: Spot on! Scratching breaks open the skin's protective shield, inviting bacteria to sneak in and cause a secondary infection.

question: Which of these is a very common field challenge when running community health programs?

options.A: Immediate willingness of all community members to participate
options.B: The complete absence of any administrative or staffing duties
options.C: Transport breakdowns and logistical delays reaching remote areas
options.D: Excessive funding that exceeds what the clinic can possibly spend

explanation: Bad roads, broken vehicles, and travel delays are classic hurdles every community health nurse learns to navigate.

question: Which set of lab tests is primarily ordered to check how well the thyroid gland is working?

options.A: Serum sodium and potassium levels
options.B: Morning cortisol and ACTH levels
options.C: Fasting glucose and HbA1c levels
options.D: TSH, T3, and T4 levels

explanation: Spot on! Checking TSH (the boss hormone from the pituitary) along with T3 and T4 (the actual thyroid hormones) gives a complete picture of thyroid health.

question: Which of these is NOT a correct nursing action when caring for a patient with an active adrenal disorder?

options.A: Monitoring strict intake, output, and daily weights to track fluid balance shifts
options.B: Educating the client on taking prescribed hormone replacement therapy consistently
options.C: Encouraging strict fluid restriction for patients experiencing an acute Addisonian crisis
options.D: Assessing for signs of infection that could trigger an acute endocrine emergency

explanation: Never restrict fluids during an Addisonian crisis! These patients have critically low blood pressure and need lots of IV fluids and sodium to bounce back safely.

question: A parent is cooking soup with a toddler playing nearby. Which simple kitchen habit prevents scalds?

options.A: Turning the pot handle inward toward the back of the stove
options.B: Leaving the pot lid slightly open so steam can escape quickly
options.C: Keeping a dry dish towel draped over the front stove knobs
options.D: Placing the pot on the front right burner for easier viewing

explanation: Exactly! Turning handles toward the back stops curious little hands from grabbing them and pulling hot food down.

question: Which genetic condition with an extra X chromosome is a common cause of low testosterone and infertility in men?

options.A: Turner syndrome
options.B: Down syndrome
options.C: Klinefelter syndrome
options.D: Cystic fibrosis

explanation: Klinefelter syndrome (47, XXY) affects testosterone production and sperm development. You're building a solid foundation in pathophysiology!

question: What is a key difference between benign and malignant tumors?

options.A: Malignant tumors stay completely contained within a capsule
options.B: Malignant tumors never grow back after simple removal
options.C: Benign tumors do not spread to distant parts of the body
options.D: Benign tumors always require immediate chemotherapy

explanation: A great way to remember this in the wards is that benign tumors stay put and grow slowly. Malignant tumors are the ones that can invade other tissues and spread around.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical barrier to effective nursing counselling?

options.A: Patient mistrust of healthcare workers
options.B: Having too much uninterrupted personal time
options.C: Language and cultural differences
options.D: Severe time constraints in busy clinics

explanation: In real-world clinics, we almost always wish we had *more* time, never too much of it!

question: What do we call a strange, unexpected drug reaction that happens because of a patient's unique genetics?

options.A: Therapeutic side effect
options.B: Anaphylactic shock
options.C: Idiosyncratic reaction
options.D: Cumulative toxicity

explanation: Idiosyncratic means it's a rare, one-of-a-kind reaction that catches everyone by surprise based on body chemistry.

question: Why do nurses avoid using chemical names of drugs during routine clinical practice?

options.A: Chemical names change every time a new company manufactures the drug
options.B: Chemical names are strictly reserved for pharmacy dispensing staff only
options.C: Chemical names are too complex and difficult to use safely in daily care
options.D: Chemical names only describe the inactive filler ingredients in the tablet

explanation: Chemical names are full of complex molecular descriptions. Imagine trying to read one out quickly during an emergency ward round—way too tricky! That's why we stick to generic and brand names.

question: What is the classic ECG sign that a heart muscle is currently injured (like in a heart attack)?

options.A: Prolonged QT interval
options.B: Flattened P waves
options.C: Shortened PR interval
options.D: ST segment elevation

explanation: When that ST segment lifts up off the line, it's a major red flag telling us the heart muscle is stressed and lacking oxygen.

question: What happens if an AED is accidentally used on someone whose heart is beating normally?

options.A: The heart will instantly stop due to the excess electrical current
options.B: The device will analyze the rhythm and refuse to deliver a shock
options.C: The machine will automatically start delivering CPR compressions
options.D: The internal battery of the device will permanently burn out

explanation: Don't worry, AEDs are very smart! They scan the heart first and will block any shock if the heart rhythm is normal. They won't harm a healthy beat.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when a patient they are monitoring suddenly becomes unresponsive?

options.A: Check responsiveness and call for emergency help
options.B: Call the attending physician to report lab results
options.C: Administer oral potassium and water
options.D: Document the exact time of the incident in the chart

explanation: In any emergency, always check if the patient responds first and get help on the way before doing anything else!

question: A mum on her second day after delivery hasn't passed stool and is scared to use the toilet. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Withhold all oral fluids and food until she passes flatus
options.B: Administer a strong stimulant enema immediately without consulting a doctor
options.C: Insist that she remains in bed until her bowel movement happens naturally
options.D: Encourage fluid intake, walking around, and check if stool softeners were ordered

explanation: Gentle movement, plenty of fluids, and stool softeners are the safest, kindest way to help her first postpartum toilet trip go smoothly!

question: What is the main reason nurses perform a nutritional assessment on a patient?

options.A: To calculate the exact cost of the patient's hospital meals
options.B: To prescribe specific dietary supplements right away
options.C: To diagnose rare genetic disorders affecting metabolism
options.D: To check nutritional status and spot any shortages or excesses early

explanation: Spotting nutritional imbalances early helps you start the right care plan before things get worse. You've got this!

question: Which disease requires you to use airborne precautions?

options.A: Acute bacterial pneumonia
options.B: Staphylococcus wound sepsis
options.C: Pulmonary tuberculosis
options.D: Simple seasonal influenza

explanation: Well done! TB is caused by tiny airborne bugs that hang suspended in the air for a long time, meaning we need special room ventilation and respirators to stay safe.

question: What does the first delay in the Three Delays Model refer to?

options.A: The time spent waiting for an ambulance on a bad road
options.B: The delay caused by nurses refusing to treat a patient
options.C: The time it takes for labor contractions to start
options.D: The delay in deciding to seek medical help

explanation: The first delay happens at the household or community level when family members fail to recognize danger signs or hesitate to seek care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h3)

question: What is the typical age range generally used to define adolescence?

options.A: 2 to 10 years
options.B: 18 to 25 years
options.C: 5 to 12 years
options.D: 10 to 19 years

explanation: Adolescence is widely defined by health organizations as the transitional period from childhood to adulthood occurring between ages 10 and 19. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for triggering the milk ejection or let-down reflex during breastfeeding?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin causes the tiny muscles around the milk glands to squeeze, pushing the milk down the ducts so the baby can drink it easily. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h1)

question: Which item belongs inside the yellow infectious waste bin during an immunization session?

options.A: Food wrappers left over from the outreach lunch break
options.B: Cardboard packaging boxes that held the vaccine vials
options.C: Cotton swabs stained with blood or vaccine fluid
options.D: Empty plastic water bottles brought by clinic staff

explanation: Items contaminated with body fluids or biological residues must go into biohazard infectious bins to prevent contamination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: Which test gives doctors the final, definitive proof of a bone cancer diagnosis?

options.A: Plain X-ray
options.B: Tissue biopsy
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Bone density scan

explanation: X-rays and scans give great clues, but looking at an actual tissue sample under a microscope (biopsy) is the gold standard for confirmation.

question: Why is it important to check the electrical cord of the steam generator before turning it on?

options.A: To verify the correct voltage for the hospital room
options.B: To measure how much electricity the unit will use
options.C: To ensure the heating water boils much faster
options.D: To prevent electrical shocks and fire hazards

explanation: Spot on! Water and electricity are a dangerous mix, so checking cords keeps both you and your patient safe.

question: Where is the best place inside a vaccine fridge to store sensitive vaccines?

options.A: On the middle shelves
options.B: Packed tight against the cooling coils
options.C: In the door storage bins
options.D: Directly on the floor panel

explanation: The middle shelves keep the most even temperature. Doors and floor areas get too many temperature swings, which can ruin the vaccines.

question: Why do nurses need to master drug dosage calculations?

options.A: To prevent medication errors and keep patients safe
options.B: To save money on pharmacy supplies
options.C: To speed up morning rounds
options.D: To skip calling the doctor

explanation: Calculations act as your final safety net to make sure patients get the exact right dose—no more, no less. You've got this!

question: What is a major safety challenge unique to home health nursing compared to working in a hospital ward?

options.A: Working alone in unsupervised, unfamiliar community environments
options.B: Lacking access to electronic health charting systems entirely
options.C: Being barred from performing physical assessments on patients
options.D: Having no responsibility for coordinating multidisciplinary care

explanation: Unlike the structured hospital ward where colleagues are close by, home health nurses often travel and enter private homes completely on their own.

question: How does a growing uterus directly cause acid reflux in expectant mothers?

options.A: By pushing the stomach upward and increasing pressure
options.B: By causing the liver to produce more digestive enzymes
options.C: By tightening the muscular walls of the esophagus
options.D: By increasing the total volume of stomach acid produced

explanation: Think of space issues! The growing womb crowds the belly and literally squeezes the stomach upward, pushing contents toward the throat.

question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the front soft spot)?

options.A: Square-shaped
options.B: Oval-shaped
options.C: Diamond-shaped
options.D: Triangle-shaped

explanation: You nailed it! The front fontanelle is larger and diamond-shaped, which makes it a great landmark to spot during an exam.

question: During a sisterhood method survey, what specific group of relatives do researchers ask about?

options.A: Older brothers and male cousins
options.B: Maternal aunts and grandmothers
options.C: Sisters who reached reproductive age
options.D: All children born in the village

explanation: Just like the name says, the sisterhood method asks adult respondents about the survival status of their sisters who reached childbearing age. Simple and clever!

question: You are caring for a patient with severe preeclampsia. Which symptom needs your immediate attention?

options.A: An oral temperature of thirty-seven degrees Celsius
options.B: A sudden report of a severe headache and blurred vision
options.C: A slight increase in anxiety about the hospital stay
options.D: A mild increase in appetite during the afternoon shift

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision in preeclampsia mean the brain is under pressure and a seizure might be near. Quick action saves lives here!

question: Which white blood cells are our most abundant and fast-acting fighters against bacteria?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Basophils
options.C: Memory cells
options.D: Eosinophils

explanation: Well done! Neutrophils are usually the very first white blood cells to rush to the scene of a fresh bacterial infection.

question: When making the initial cut to drain an abscess, which direction should the surgical blade follow?

options.A: Directly perpendicular to muscle fibers
options.B: In a randomized zigzag pattern
options.C: Along the natural skin tension lines
options.D: In a wide circular shape around the border

explanation: Cutting along the body's natural skin lines (Langer's lines) helps the wound heal better and keeps scarring to a minimum.

question: A patient gets widespread hives, mild wheezing, and belly cramps 10 minutes after an antibiotic. What kind of reaction is this?

options.A: Moderate
options.B: Delayed
options.C: Severe
options.D: Mild

explanation: When symptoms affect more than one body part—like both the skin and the tummy—we classify it as moderate.

question: What is the main advantage of an interprofessional healthcare team for an elderly patient?

options.A: Lower overall healthcare costs for the government
options.B: Comprehensive care that improves overall quality of life
options.C: Faster discharge from acute care hospitals
options.D: Elimination of the need for informal family caregivers

explanation: When different health professionals combine their skills, all aspects of the patient's physical, emotional, and social needs get covered, leading to happier, healthier days.

question: What do we call an abnormal, new growth of tissue that forms a tumor?

options.A: Atrophy
options.B: Neoplasm
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Great start! A neoplasm is simply an abnormal mass of tissue that grows when cells divide more than they should. Think 'neo' (new) + 'plasma' (formation). You've got this!

question: Why can it be dangerous when two different drugs compete for the exact same CYP450 enzyme?

options.A: It turns every medication into a harmful poison immediately
options.B: It can cause one drug to build up to toxic levels because its breakdown is delayed
options.C: It prevents the stomach from absorbing any water or nutrients
options.D: It instantly stops all blood flow to the kidneys and liver

explanation: Imagine two cars trying to pass through a single-lane toll gate. If the enzymes are busy clearing Drug A, Drug B has to wait in line, builds up in the blood, and can cause toxicity!

question: Roughly what percentage of a healthy adult's body weight is water?

options.A: 60 percent
options.B: 5 percent
options.C: 90 percent
options.D: 20 percent

explanation: Water makes up about 60% of an adult body! It is the fluid highway where almost all cellular activities happen.

question: What is the absolute number one priority when managing a patient with a suspected drug overdose?

options.A: Securing the airway and ensuring breathing
options.B: Administering a laxative to clear the bowels
options.C: Finding out the exact name of the drug taken
options.D: Filling out the hospital admission forms

explanation: Remember your ABCs! In any emergency, stabilizing the airway, breathing, and circulation always comes before playing detective to find out what happened.

question: Which reflex is NOT coordinated by the medulla oblongata?

options.A: The swallowing reflex
options.B: The coughing reflex
options.C: The vomiting reflex
options.D: Visual tracking of a moving object

explanation: Visual tracking is handled by higher brain areas and midbrain structures, whereas vomiting, swallowing, and coughing are medullary reflexes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: Which psychological condition is often seen in women and girls who have survived FGM?

options.A: Bipolar manic depression with hallucinations
options.B: Obsessive compulsive cleaning disorder
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder and anxiety
options.D: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder

explanation: Spot on! The painful and terrifying experience often leaves survivors with long-term emotional trauma, anxiety, and distress.

question: Why does liver disease often lead to body swelling and fluid buildup?

options.A: The liver fails to destroy excess red blood cells.
options.B: The liver blocks the main lymphatic channels in the abdomen.
options.C: The liver stops producing enough blood proteins to maintain oncotic pressure.
options.D: Damaged liver cells pump too much salt directly into the bloodstream.

explanation: Exactly! The liver is our protein factory. When it's sick, it can't make enough albumin, meaning fluid escapes the blood vessels easily and causes swelling.

question: What is a flat, colored spot on the skin that is less than 1 cm wide called?

options.A: Papule
options.B: Plaque
options.C: Vesicle
options.D: Macule

explanation: Think of a simple freckle or flat mole—that's a macule! It's just a flat, colored spot on the skin.

question: A young child comes in with frequent diarrhea, slow growth, and wounds that take too long to heal. Which deficiency is most likely the cause?

options.A: Iodine
options.B: Iron
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Zinc

explanation: Well done! Zinc is a superstar for a child's immune system, gut health, and growth. When it's low, healing and recovery slow down. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why do we call dietetics both a science and an art?

options.A: It involves laboratory experiments and painting patient charts
options.B: It relies entirely on guesswork rather than research
options.C: It uses artistic portraits to track weight loss
options.D: It requires scientific calculations and creative meal planning

explanation: Great thinking! Dietitians use hard science for nutritional calculations, but they also need creativity to make meal plans fit real human lives, budgets, and cultural preferences.

question: Why must a nurse carefully watch a patient's urine output after starting an anticholinergic anti-spasmodic?

options.A: The drug is filtered out very rapidly by the kidneys
options.B: It prevents the patient from developing severe diarrhea
options.C: It proves the drug is successfully relaxing the stomach
options.D: The medication can cause urinary retention

explanation: Anticholinergics can make it hard for the bladder to squeeze properly, causing urine to get trapped. Always keep an eye on how well your patient is passing urine!

question: How many total antenatal visits does the World Health Organization recommend for a normal, healthy pregnancy?

options.A: At least eight contacts
options.B: Exactly four visits
options.C: Only one per trimester
options.D: Twelve monthly visits

explanation: Global health guidelines recommend a minimum of eight antenatal visits so moms and babies get optimal monitoring and support throughout the journey.

question: How does drying (dehydration) primarily preserve food?

options.A: By keeping the food at freezing cold temperatures
options.B: By increasing the internal oxygen levels of the food
options.C: By adding large amounts of chemical preservatives
options.D: By removing the water that microorganisms need to grow

explanation: Think of it this way: germs need water to survive and multiply, just like we do. Take the water away, and they can't grow!

question: What key advice should a nurse give a patient starting daily levothyroxine?

options.A: Swallow the tablet with an antacid to protect your stomach lining.
options.B: Avoid taking the pill if your heart rate is above 90 beats per minute.
options.C: Take the dose right after a large evening meal to prevent nausea.
options.D: Take the medication on an empty stomach in the morning.

explanation: Well done! Food, iron, and calcium can trap levothyroxine in the gut, so taking it first thing on an empty stomach ensures the body absorbs it properly.

question: What is the very first step of urine formation in the kidney?

options.A: Tubular secretion
options.B: Glomerular filtration
options.C: Peristaltic propulsion
options.D: Tubular reabsorption

explanation: Everything starts at the glomerulus! Blood pressure forces water and small particles out of the blood and into Bowman's capsule to kick off urine making.

question: Why is it better to call for an emergency medical assistance team early instead of waiting for a full cardiac arrest?

options.A: It reduces the cost of hospital medications.
options.B: It keeps the hospital hallways quiet during visiting hours.
options.C: It prevents doctors from having to do paperwork later.
options.D: It allows the team to treat the underlying cause before the heart stops.

explanation: Once a patient's heart stops, their chance of surviving intact drops significantly compared to catching and fixing the problem while they still have a pulse. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of low blood potassium that a nurse should watch for?

options.A: Sudden uncontrollable shaking of the hands
options.B: Irregular heart rhythms
options.C: Muscle cramps and weakness
options.D: Extreme fatigue and lethargy

explanation: Muscle cramps, tiredness, and irregular heartbeats are classic signs of low potassium. Hand tremors point to other issues, not hypokalemia!

question: Why is an unsafe injection a big deal in public health?

options.A: It almost always leads to immediate surgical site infections
options.B: It causes severe allergic reactions in every patient who receives it
options.C: It can easily transmit serious bloodborne infections to healthy individuals
options.D: It guarantees that the administered drug will not work properly

explanation: Unsafe practices bypass the skin's natural defenses, which can directly spread heavy infections like HIV and hepatitis into the bloodstream.

question: Why should you ask a patient to close their eyes during a sensory touch test?

options.A: To measure if the patient can stay awake under stress
options.B: To prevent visual cues from helping them guess the stimulus
options.C: To help the patient fall asleep during a long examination
options.D: To protect the eyes from bright room lights and glare

explanation: Closing their eyes ensures they rely purely on their nerves and touch, rather than cheating by peeking at what you are doing!

question: As a nurse assessing patient movements, what do you call moving a limb away from the midline of the body?

options.A: Flexion
options.B: Abduction
options.C: Adduction
options.D: Pronation

explanation: Spot on! When you 'abduct' something, you take it away—just like lifting your arm up away from your side.

question: What is the main type of tissue found in the hypodermis (the layer right under the skin)?

options.A: Adipose tissue
options.B: Dense regular connective tissue
options.C: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.D: Nervous tissue

explanation: Correct! The hypodermis is mostly made of adipose (fat) tissue, which keeps us warm, stores energy, and cushions our organs.

question: What is the main job of a flight nurse?

options.A: Repairing aircraft engines and systems
options.B: Piloting emergency medical helicopters
options.C: Managing hospital intensive care units
options.D: Providing medical care during aircraft transport

explanation: You've got this! Flight nurses specialize in looking after patients and giving continuous medical care while flying in an aircraft. Simple and vital!

question: Why is it clinically important to know that testicular lymph drains to lumbar nodes while scrotal lymph drains to inguinal nodes?

options.A: It dictates how different reproductive cancers spread through the body.
options.B: It dictates the correct dosage for local anesthetic blocks.
options.C: It explains why inguinal hernias occur in older adults.
options.D: It determines how much testosterone the adrenal glands release.

explanation: Cancer metastasis pathways follow lymphatic drainage, making the distinct drainage routes crucial for staging scrotal versus testicular malignancies. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which chart is commonly used in the clinic to test a patient's eyesight?

options.A: Tonometer
options.B: Snellen chart
options.C: Audiometer
options.D: Ophthalmoscope

explanation: The Snellen chart is the classic eye chart with rows of letters that get smaller and smaller. It's the standard tool nurses and doctors use to check visual acuity!

question: Why is treating a degenerative illness very different from treating a sudden bacterial infection?

options.A: Medications for degenerative conditions never have side effects
options.B: Infection drugs kill the invading germs, while degenerative drugs manage long-term loss
options.C: Infections are genetic, while degenerative diseases are caught from other people
options.D: Infections need lifelong management while degenerative diseases need short antibiotics

explanation: Spot on! An antibiotic can knock out an infection completely, but chronic degenerative conditions need ongoing care because the body's tissues are slowly breaking down over time.

question: When are most anthelminthic drugs strictly avoided due to risks to the baby?

options.A: During the final weeks of breastfeeding
options.B: During the first trimester of pregnancy
options.C: In patients over sixty-five years of age
options.D: Throughout the entire adolescent period

explanation: Spot on! Since the baby's vital organs are forming during the first trimester, we generally avoid these drugs to keep the foetus safe.

question: What is a 'windshield survey' in community nursing?

options.A: Checking vehicle exhaust fumes to measure air pollution levels
options.B: Observing a community firsthand by walking or driving through it
options.C: Testing the driving vision of commercial vehicle drivers
options.D: Administering a written questionnaire to hospital patients

explanation: Imagine driving or walking slowly through a neighborhood just observing houses, trash disposal, and daily life. That's a windshield survey!

question: How do doctors usually confirm a diagnosis of Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: An electrical muscle test of the upper and lower limbs
options.B: A simple finger-prick blood glucose test done at the bedside
options.C: Clinical history, neurological assessment, and neuroimaging
options.D: A 24-hour urine collection measuring total protein content

explanation: Since there isn't one quick blood test for it, clinicians look at the patient's story, test their memory, and use brain scans like an MRI.

question: Which common group of over-the-counter painkillers must patients with kidney disease strictly avoid?

options.A: Plain acetaminophen tablets
options.B: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.C: Multivitamins with vitamin C
options.D: Antacids containing calcium

explanation: NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or diclofenac) can severely cut off blood flow to struggling kidneys and cause even more damage. Always watch out for them in kidney patients!

question: Which clinical signs are classic clues that a patient's liver is struggling to excrete bilirubin properly?

options.A: Dark urine and pale, clay-colored stools
options.B: Extreme sensitivity to bright outdoor light
options.C: Bright red spots scattered over the chest
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: Think about the pathway: if bile can't reach the intestines, stool loses its brown colour, and the excess bilirubin spills out through the kidneys, making the urine very dark.

question: The telemetry alarm sounds and the screen shows a wild, chaotic line, but the patient is sitting up calmly talking on the phone. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Check the patient and inspect the electrode connections
options.B: Call the doctor immediately to report ventricular fibrillation
options.C: Bring the crash cart to the bedside and prepare to shock
options.D: Turn off the monitor alarm permanently to reduce noise

explanation: Always assess the patient and check the equipment for loose leads before acting on a potentially false reading. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is getting religious and traditional leaders involved so important for ending FGM?

options.A: They control the financial budgets of state health ministries
options.B: They have the constitutional power to write federal laws
options.C: They hold strong moral authority and influence how community members behave
options.D: They are legally required to do routine medical checkups

explanation: Correct! People deeply respect traditional and religious leaders, so when they speak out against FGM, it drives real behavior change.

question: What key fact should nurses explain to adolescents about emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: They provide full immunity against all known sexually transmitted diseases
options.B: They must be taken every single morning to maintain long-term effectiveness
options.C: They guarantee that future menstrual cycles will arrive on the exact same day
options.D: They do not interrupt an established pregnancy or act as an abortifacient

explanation: Emergency contraceptives simply delay ovulation; they don't harm an egg that has already implanted.

question: Which lab test is usually ordered to check if hormones are causing a patient's sexual difficulties?

options.A: Serum calcium
options.B: Serum testosterone
options.C: Urinalysis culture
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: You got it! Checking serum testosterone levels lets us see if low hormone production is the culprit behind the struggle.

question: What is the main goal of doing regular skin self-examinations?

options.A: Detecting skin abnormalities at an early, treatable stage
options.B: Restoring lost moisture to severely dry epidermal layers
options.C: Completely preventing any future skin injuries from occurring
options.D: Eliminating the need for daily hygiene and moisturizing

explanation: Spot on! Catching skin changes early means any issues can be treated quickly before they turn into something serious.

question: A client started birth control pills two weeks ago and comes back worried about mild, irregular spotting. What should you do first as her nurse?

options.A: Prescribe a high-dose antibiotic to treat a presumed uterine infection
options.B: Refer her urgently to a surgeon for an exploratory pelvic examination
options.C: Advise her to stop taking the medication immediately and switch to surgical sterilization
options.D: Reassure her that irregular spotting is normal during the first few months of adjustment

explanation: Spot on! Early spotting is very common when the body is getting used to new hormones. A little reassurance goes a long way while her body adjusts.

question: A patient says they feel completely full after eating just two spoonfuls of porridge. What is likely happening?

options.A: Rapid healing of the stomach lining
options.B: An allergic reaction to the specific ingredients
options.C: A sudden surge in physical metabolism
options.D: Early satiety caused by slowed digestive function

explanation: Exactly! When digestion slows down in advanced illness, the stomach fills up extremely fast—a concept we call 'early satiety'.

question: What is recognized as the single most effective nursing action to prevent the spread of infections?

options.A: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Spraying chemical disinfectants on floors
options.C: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.D: Placing all patients in isolation rooms

question: Which of these is a MISTAKE when getting a patient ready for a digital blood pressure check?

options.A: Making sure both of the patient's feet are flat on the floor
options.B: Asking the patient to stay quiet while the machine runs
options.C: Allowing the patient to keep a thick sweater on with the cuff rolled over it
options.D: Ensuring the patient rests quietly for five minutes beforehand

explanation: Always put the cuff directly on bare skin! Thick clothing or tight rolling can pinch the arm and mess up your numbers.

question: A care assistant is about to feed a resident who has trouble swallowing. What safety tip should you give?

options.A: Offer large chunks of solid food for better chewing
options.B: Feed the resident as quickly as possible
options.C: Position the resident in an upright sitting posture
options.D: Encourage the resident to lie flat on the bed

explanation: Brilliant! Sitting upright uses gravity to help swallowing and keeps food out of the lungs, preventing dangerous choking.

question: What is a major risk to a newborn if the mother receives strong pain opioids right before delivery?

options.A: Neonatal respiratory depression
options.B: Rapid premature bone growth
options.C: Severe congenital heart defects
options.D: Permanent hearing impairment

explanation: If opioids cross the placenta just before birth, the baby might be born a bit too sleepy to take a good first breath on their own.

question: What is one of the biggest risks when wheeling a critical patient away for an advanced scan?

options.A: Permanent discoloration of the patient's skin
options.B: Accidental dislodgement of breathing tubes and lines
options.C: Automatic deletion of electronic health records
options.D: Sudden freezing of the hospital computed tomography machine

explanation: Moving beds down hallways and shifting patients onto imaging tables puts a lot of stress on delicate IV lines and breathing tubes.

question: A male patient insists he doesn't have an STI because his sores don't hurt. How should you gently correct him?

options.A: Painlessness proves that the infection is restricted to the skin surface only
options.B: Some serious infections like syphilis can cause painless sores in their early stages
options.C: If a lesion does not hurt, the body will eliminate the virus automatically
options.D: Painless sores always indicate a non-infectious skin allergy rather than an STI

explanation: It's a common trap! Remind your patients that a lack of pain does not mean lack of disease—syphilis chancres are notorious for being painless.

question: What is the medical term for a lack of oxygen to an unborn baby?

options.A: Placental abruption
options.B: Foetal hyperglycemia
options.C: Intrauterine hypoxia
options.D: Uterine hyperstimulation

question: Why should you place dentures back in a patient's mouth before family viewing, unless policy says otherwise?

options.A: It helps restore a natural facial appearance for the grieving family
options.B: Hospital regulations require all medical devices to remain intact
options.C: It prevents the jaw from locking shut during rigor mortis
options.D: It makes the body easier to transport to the mortuary van

explanation: Putting dentures in helps the patient look like themselves, which can bring a little bit of comfort to grieving family members.

question: Why is a laryngoscopy done?

options.A: It takes X-rays of the chest and inflates collapsed lung tissue simultaneously.
options.B: It measures blood pressure in the throat and delivers emergency oral medications.
options.C: It cures chronic lung infections and removes foreign bodies from the stomach.
options.D: It checks voice box issues and also helps place breathing tubes during resuscitation.

explanation: Exactly! It's a handy tool both for figuring out throat problems and for guiding breathing tubes when someone needs emergency help.

question: A pregnant patient with hyperemesis has low potassium and high blood pH. What is happening?

options.A: Respiratory acidosis
options.B: Metabolic acidosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

explanation: Pumping out stomach acid through continuous vomiting strips the body of hydrogen ions, causing blood pH to rise. That's metabolic alkalosis in action—keep smashing those lab values!

question: What is the medical term for the hard bumps of urate crystals that form under the skin in long-standing gout?

options.A: Tophi
options.B: Vesicle
options.C: Nodule
options.D: Pannus

explanation: Tophi are those visible lumps of uric acid crystals that can pop up under the skin or around joints when gout isn't well controlled over time.

question: Why do nurses take a baseline set of vital signs when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: It gives a standard reference point to detect future clinical changes
options.B: It prevents the patient from developing hospital-acquired infections
options.C: It determines the exact medical diagnosis without needing lab tests
options.D: It fulfills the legal requirement to discharge the patient safely

explanation: Having an accurate starting measurement helps you immediately spot when your patient's condition starts getting worse. Great job thinking like a nurse! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h1)

question: What is the usual time gap between taking mifepristone and misoprostol?

options.A: Exactly one week apart
options.B: 24 to 48 hours
options.C: Immediately at the same time
options.D: 12 to 14 days apart

explanation: You'll often see 24 to 48 hours prescribed—this gives the first drug enough time to do its job so the second drug can work effectively.

question: Why do patients dealing with chronic pain often have terrible sleep problems?

options.A: Physical pain forces the brain to produce excessive amounts of melatonin.
options.B: Analgesic medications always cause permanent destruction of REM sleep cycles.
options.C: Pain triggers physical discomfort that prevents the nervous system from relaxing into sleep.
options.D: Chronic pain completely eliminates the need for stage three sleep.

explanation: Constant physical discomfort acts like a stress alarm, keeping the nervous system fired up and making it really hard to slip into deep, continuous sleep.

question: What happens to a joint capsule when severe inflammation occurs?

options.A: It completely dries up and fuses the bones together
options.B: It stops producing all blood supply to the limb
options.C: It produces excess fluid, creating a joint effusion
options.D: It turns into hard bone tissue overnight

explanation: Inflammation inside the joint lining triggers swelling and fluid buildup, which is called an effusion. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h2)

question: How is evaluation different from daily monitoring in a health program?

options.A: Evaluation only tracks financial expenditures and purchasing receipts
options.B: Evaluation is handled exclusively by international donor agencies
options.C: Evaluation happens every morning before project activities begin
options.D: Evaluation is a periodic assessment of overall project outcomes and impact

question: A nurse notices that the cleaning staff plugged an electric kettle into the same socket used for the vaccine refrigerator. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Leave both plugged in as long as the electricity is stable
options.B: Unplug the kettle and ensure the refrigerator has a dedicated socket
options.C: Move the kettle to another room only when patients are present
options.D: Switch off the refrigerator while the kettle is boiling water

question: Why are pediatric medication doses usually calculated based on the child's body weight?

options.A: Weight calculations are only used for intravenous drugs, not oral ones
options.B: Children's body composition and organ maturity differ greatly from adults
options.C: Children refuse to swallow pills that weigh more than a certain amount
options.D: Hospital pharmacies only stock liquid medicines in weight-based bottles

question: What is the primary focus of neurological nursing?

options.A: Managing surgical procedures on the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Treating chronic lung and respiratory infections
options.C: Monitoring and caring for clients with nervous system disorders
options.D: Providing long-term physical therapy for broken bones

explanation: Neurological nursing centers entirely on assessing, monitoring, and supporting clients experiencing problems with the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h1)

question: How should you write entries in a permanent clinic register to keep records safe and professional?

options.A: In shorthand code that only the head nurse understands
options.B: Neatly in ink without unauthorized erasures
options.C: In pencil so mistakes can be easily rubbed out
options.D: Using colored markers to make pages look bright

question: What medication is given immediately to reverse a heparin overdose?

options.A: Protamine sulfate
options.B: Vitamin K tablets

options.D: Calcium gluconate

explanation: Protamine sulfate is the fast-acting antidote that neutralizes heparin right away in an emergency. You're doing amazing!

question: What should you do if a patient cannot remember the names of their home medications?

options.A: Disregard home drugs and start fresh hospital drugs
options.B: Guess the medications based on their visible disease symptoms
options.C: Scold the patient for being careless with their health

question: Why is emotional support such a big part of nursing care after an abortion or miscarriage?

options.A: Emotional counseling completely eliminates the risk of physical infection
options.B: Patients often experience complex grief, anxiety, and psychological distress
options.C: Psychological support replaces the need for vital sign monitoring
options.D: Hormonal changes only affect physical health and never mental well-being

explanation: Losing a pregnancy hurts deeply on the inside. Being a warm, listening nurse is just as important as checking physical vitals!

question: Why was a new law like the VAPP Act urgently needed when older criminal codes already existed?

options.A: Older laws required permission from international courts.

options.C: Older laws only applied to children and the elderly.

question: What is a very common underlying cause of autonomic neuropathy in clinical practice?

question: Why must you record it carefully when a client decides to switch their contraceptive method?

options.A: To prove that the previous contraceptive method caused a severe illness

options.C: To prevent inaccurate tallying and avoid double-counting service statistics

explanation: You got it! Tracking method switches properly keeps our numbers honest and stops us from accidentally counting the same person twice.

question: Why is early recognition of genitourinary growths so important?

options.A: It directly improves survival rates and quality of life
options.B: It guarantees that the tumor will remain completely benign
options.C: It completely prevents the need for any future blood tests
options.D: It ensures the patient will never require surgical intervention

question: Why is performing last offices calmly so important for the family?

options.B: It prevents the family from asking too many questions

options.D: It proves to the doctor that death actually occurred

question: In community health nursing, who is considered your primary client?

options.A: The individual patient

question: Why is proper technique so important when doing venepuncture?

options.C: To prevent patient harm and protect sample quality

question: Why does maternal hyperglycemia lead to macrosomia in the developing fetus?

question: Where are the kidneys located in the human body?

question: Why is it important to check blood clotting lab results before a dilation procedure?

question: How does a hiatus hernia make acid reflux worse?

question: Which set of findings represents standard vital signs taken during a routine check?

question: Why is educating community and religious leaders an effective way to fight child trafficking?

question: A client in a Nigerian teaching hospital demands to see their medical case notes after a surgery. How should the nurse respond?

options.B: Refuse firmly because hospital files belong exclusively to the doctors and nurses

question: What is a common sign of 'silent aspiration' in someone with swallowing difficulties?

question: What is the role of the ductus venosus in the baby's abdomen?

question: What is the primary physiological mechanism that causes pressure injuries to form over bony prominences?

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation nursing compared to acute care?

question: When is the best time to perform airway suctioning on a ventilated patient?

question: Which phrase is an example of unhelpful communication when talking to a dying patient?

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse would typically do regarding female reproductive health?

question: What is the main goal of community-based accident prevention programs?

question: Why is community outreach considered a key component of youth-friendly health services?

question: Why does a nurse perform a head-to-toe examination instead of only checking the patient's main complaint?

question: Why is it dangerous to combine certain azoles with blood thinners like warfarin?

question: What does 'informed consent' actually mean for a client undergoing a health screening?

question: Which of these is a life-threatening emergency caused by severely out-of-control diabetes?

question: When the parasympathetic nervous system kicks in, what happens to your heart rate?

question: Why is it important for assisted living homes to balance safety rules with personal freedom?

question: Why are non-benzodiazepine sleeping pills so popular for short-term insomnia?

question: A patient keeps visiting the clinic with headaches and stomach upset, but all lab tests come out normal. What should you suspect?

question: Why must instrument box locks and ratchets be kept open during the sterilization process?

question: Which type of patient needs a full-body mechanical lift?

question: A community nurse wants to store the medical history of a husband, wife, and their children together in one file. Which stationery item should be used?

question: Why is cancer staging so important after a patient receives a confirmed diagnosis?

question: What is the best way to talk to a patient who is frantic and overwhelmed in the emergency room?

question: What is the primary role of the instructor during a debriefing session?

question: What legal charge might you face if you force medication on a clear-headed adult patient who says no?

question: Why might a patient experience a sudden dangerous drop in heart rate during suctioning?

question: Which family dynamic is most strongly linked to an increased risk of early unprotected sex in teens?

question: What is personal invulnerability in the context of adolescent psychology?

question: What is the most important first step in managing any patient diagnosed with an occupational lung disease?

question: What is the main job of angiotensin II in the body?

question: A patient tells you they stopped taking their daily allopurinol because their toe stopped hurting. What is your best nursing advice?

question: What is an important assessment to do BEFORE starting steam therapy?

question: A patient with severe liver disease looks restless, seems confused, and has a fast heart rate with dropping blood pressure. What should the nurse do first?

question: How does Crohn's disease affect the bowel wall differently from Ulcerative Colitis?

options.C: To leave space for semen and prevent bursting
options.D: To warm up the latex material

explanation: You got it! Pinching the tip pushes out trapped air and leaves a little room to catch the semen so the condom doesn't tear.

question: When is the risk of maternal and newborn complications highest after delivery?

options.A: After the sixth month
options.B: Within the first 48 hours
options.C: Around the second year
options.D: During the fourth week

explanation: Exactly! The first 48 hours after birth require our closest attention because heavy bleeding or infections can happen quickly.

question: During a neuro exam, why do nurses check different parts of the body instead of just the head?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory paperwork requirements for hospital accreditation
options.B: Because the nervous system controls functions across the entire body
options.C: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the evaluation
options.D: Because peripheral nerves operate completely independently of the brain

explanation: Nerves reach everywhere—from your head down to your toes. That's why a problem in the nervous system can show up as changes all over the body!

question: Which skin receptor is especially good at sensing deep pressure and fast vibrations?

options.A: Free nerve ending
options.B: Merkel disc
options.C: Meissner's corpuscle
options.D: Pacinian corpuscle

explanation: Spot on! Pacinian corpuscles are deep in the dermis and act like tiny sensors for strong pressure and vibrations.

question: A doctor writes a medication dose that looks obviously incorrect for your patient. What should you do?

options.A: Ask a junior colleague to give the drug so blame is shared
options.B: Administer the medication quickly so care isn't delayed
options.C: Ignore the order completely and document nothing
options.D: Clarify the order with the prescriber before giving the medication

explanation: Brilliant! Patient safety comes first. Always pause to clarify any unsafe or confusing orders before you administer anything.

question: During a hysterosalpingography (HSG) procedure, what is injected into the uterus to make the tubes visible on an X-ray?

options.A: Sterile normal saline
options.B: Liquid medical silicone
options.C: Radioactive glucose solution
options.D: Radiopaque contrast dye

explanation: Doctors use a special contrast dye so that X-ray machines can clearly trace the fluid as it flows through the womb and down the fallopian tubes.

question: Why is observing chest symmetry important during the breathing assessment?

options.A: It tells the nurse if the patient has a chronic respiratory infection
options.B: It determines whether the patient has eaten recently
options.C: It helps detect uneven lung expansion caused by injury or trapped air
options.D: It is the only way to calculate the exact respiratory rate accurately

explanation: Asymmetrical chest movement often points to serious problems like a pneumothorax, flail chest, or hemothorax requiring immediate intervention. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h4)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do with a mechanical weighing scale before a patient steps on it?

options.A: Wipe the platform with hot cooking oil
options.B: Place a thick mat underneath it
options.C: Lock the height rod permanently
options.D: Calibrate and balance it to zero

explanation: Always check that the scale starts right at zero! This ensures your weight reading is accurate and not thrown off by a previous reading.

question: What standard framework guides disease reporting forms in Nigerian health facilities?

options.A: Standard Operating Procedures for Pharmacy Inventory
options.B: National Curriculum for Basic Nursing Education
options.C: Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR)
options.D: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)

explanation: IDSR is the golden framework we use across Nigerian facilities to keep our disease tracking organized and consistent. You'll see this a lot in practice!

question: A dying patient is struggling to catch their breath and looks very anxious. What simple, comforting action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Position the patient flat on their back
options.B: Insert a rigid plastic breathing tube
options.C: Administer a strong sleeping pill by mouth
options.D: Direct a small electric fan to blow gentle air toward their face

explanation: A gentle breeze across the face stimulates facial nerves that quickly help calm the feeling of breathlessness. It's a wonderful, non-invasive nursing comfort measure! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care when using the concept of basic human needs?

options.A: Discharging the patient as quickly as possible
options.B: Focusing on the whole person and their essential requirements
options.C: Treating only the diagnosed disease process
options.D: Managing hospital administrative tasks

explanation: Looking at basic human needs helps nurses care for the entire individual rather than just treating a specific illness. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: How do typical skin lesions of Kaposi sarcoma look?

options.A: Painful, red ulcers with a yellow base
options.B: Itchy, fluid-filled vesicular clusters
options.C: Scaly, silvery plaques with dry edges
options.D: Painless, purplish or brownish nodules

explanation: Skin lesions from Kaposi sarcoma usually show up as distinct, firm, and painless spots or bumps that look purple, pink, or brown.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of chronic osteomyelitis?

options.A: Instantaneous paralysis of the affected limb
options.B: A sudden high fever with no local pain whatsoever
options.C: Complete numbness and coldness in the toes
options.D: A draining sinus tract leaking pus onto the skin

explanation: A sinus tract is a little tunnel that forms from the infected bone out to the skin, constantly draining pus. A classic clinical clue!

question: What actually causes that sharp, terrible pain and swelling during a gout flare?

options.A: Complete wearing away of the cartilage
options.B: Sudden thickening of the synovial fluid
options.C: Uric acid crystals building up in the joint
options.D: A bacterial infection inside the joint capsule

explanation: You've got this! When uric acid piles up, it forms needle-like crystals in the joint. Your body's immune system attacks these crystals, leading to that fiery pain and swelling.

question: What should a nursing unit manager do immediately after setting targets with the staff?

options.A: Punish nurses who ask questions about the goals
options.B: File the document away until the end of the year
options.C: Hand over all leadership duties to junior staff
options.D: Support staff in carrying out daily duties toward those targets

explanation: After goals are set, the actual work phase begins where staff execute plans and management provides support. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is a vital disease-prevention shot routinely given during pregnancy clinics in Nigeria?

options.A: Insulin pump placement
options.B: Tetanus toxoid vaccination
options.C: Chemotherapy infusion
options.D: Joint replacement surgery

explanation: Well done! Tetanus toxoid is a routine life-saver given during pregnancy to protect both the mother and newborn baby from tetanus.

question: What is the minimum number of generations a nurse should typically explore when taking a family health history?

options.A: Five generations
options.B: Only one generation
options.C: Three generations
options.D: Ten generations

explanation: Looking back across three generations (parents, children, and grandparents) helps reveal hidden inheritance patterns of hereditary conditions. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h3)

question: Why must an adult patient fast before having an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy?

options.A: To make sure the patient loses weight during the hospital stay
options.B: To speed up the action of the sedative medication
options.C: To prevent the camera from heating up inside the stomach
options.D: To prevent aspiration of stomach contents into the lungs

explanation: Safety first! An empty stomach ensures the patient won't vomit and accidentally breathe food or liquid into their lungs while sedated.

question: Why do doctors and nurses prefer ultrasound when a patient needs repeated scans over a short time?

options.A: it does not use harmful ionizing radiation
options.B: It is totally painless and needs no practice
options.C: It gives a much clearer view of bones than a CT scan
options.D: It completely replaces the need for blood tests

explanation: Because it lacks harmful radiation, ultrasound is super safe and can be repeated as many times as needed to monitor healing.

question: What is a major advantage of administering drugs through the rectum?

options.A: It can be used effectively when a patient is actively vomiting
options.B: It guarantees 100 percent predictable absorption every time
options.C: It is always the preferred choice for alert adult patients
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any hand hygiene

explanation: When oral drugs cannot be kept down due to vomiting, the rectal route ensures the patient still receives necessary treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h3)

question: What do we call a tumor that has traveled to the brain from another part of the body, like the lungs?

options.A: Benign tumor
options.B: Primary tumor
options.C: Metastatic tumor
options.D: Congenital tumor

explanation: You've got this! When cancer cells break away from a spot like the breast or lungs and travel to the brain, we call it a metastatic (or secondary) tumor. Think of it as a traveler from another part of the body.

question: How do specialized support cohorts differ from standard general groups?

options.A: They focus on the unique life challenges of specific populations like adolescents or pregnant women.
options.B: They require mandatory financial contributions from every attending member.
options.C: They meet exclusively inside high-security hospital surgical wards.
options.D: They exclude anyone who has been on antiretroviral medication for more than one year.

explanation: Specialized cohorts target specific groups so members can discuss challenges unique to their life stage or medical condition. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h2)

question: Peptic ulcer treatment usually focuses on balancing which two opposing forces in the stomach?

options.A: Red blood cell counts and white blood cell counts
options.B: Dietary sugar intake and physical exercise levels
options.C: Fluid intake and urinary output volume
options.D: Aggressive acid factors and defensive mucosal factors

explanation: Think of it as a tug-of-war! Strong acid tries to damage the stomach, while the stomach's natural mucus tries to protect it. Drugs help restore that balance.

question: Which of the following is NOT a nurse's role in community Family Life Education?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations in schools
options.B: Acting as an advocate for adolescent health
options.C: Serving as an educator for health promotion
options.D: Counseling families on resource availability

explanation: Nurses do not do surgeries in schools! Our focus is on health education, counseling, and supporting our clients.

question: Which stage of dementia usually lasts the longest and is known for noticeable confusion and wandering?

options.A: Pre-clinical stage
options.B: Early stage
options.C: Middle stage
options.D: Late stage

explanation: The middle stage is typically the longest. It brings clear behavioral changes, like wandering and needing help with daily tasks.

question: Why does a lack of health awareness stop patients from insisting on safe injections?

options.A: They have enough money to buy private syringes
options.B: They prefer taking bitter oral medications instead
options.C: They understand hospital sterilization protocols fully
options.D: They do not know what hazards to look out for

explanation: You nailed it. If a patient doesn't know the risks, they won't know what dangerous practices to watch out for or what to demand.

question: Which protective layer of the meninges wraps directly and tightly around the surface of the spinal cord?

options.A: Pia mater
options.B: Arachnoid mater
options.C: Periosteum
options.D: Dura mater

explanation: Great job! The pia mater is the innermost, delicate layer that hugs every single curve and groove of the spinal cord and brain like a second skin.

question: Which tools do clinics primarily use to track when a family planning client is due back?

options.A: Daily weather monitoring charts
options.B: Appointment registers and individual client cards
options.C: Pharmacy inventory bills for unrelated drugs
options.D: National television broadcast schedules

explanation: Client cards and clinic registers are our best friends for keeping track of return dates so no one slips through the cracks.

question: Which acute complication is caused by severe lack of insulin, leading to acid buildup and ketones in Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
options.B: Peripheral neuropathy
options.C: Severe hypoglycemia
options.D: Diabetic ketoacidosis

explanation: When cells can't get glucose without insulin, the body burns fat instead. This process makes acidic byproducts called ketones, causing diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). You're tackling advanced concepts like a pro!

question: Which family planning method also protects against sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Progestin-only pills
options.B: Subdermal hormone implants
options.C: Copper intrauterine devices
options.D: Barrier methods

explanation: Condoms and other barrier methods are great because they do double duty: they prevent pregnancy and block infections too!

question: Which organ gets overwhelmed and converts surplus dietary sugars into fat?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Kidneys
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Liver

explanation: Your liver handles the heavy lifting when processing dietary sugars. When it gets overloaded, it converts those extra sugars directly into fat molecules.

question: Why is a luminal medication also prescribed along with tissue-active drugs?

options.A: To replace lost electrolytes and boost red blood cell production
options.B: To permanently numb the lining of the stomach against acid
options.C: To speed up the healing of skin lesions on the abdomen
options.D: To clear remaining cysts from the bowel lumen and prevent relapse

explanation: Exactly! While one drug clears the tissues, the luminal agent mops up any cysts left in the gut so the infection doesn't bounce back.

question: What is the main purpose of the initial evaluation phase in rehabilitation?

options.A: Discharging the patient permanently to their home
options.B: Identifying baseline functional deficits and recovery potential
options.C: Initiating high-impact athletic training
options.D: Stopping all medications to test natural healing

explanation: Before planning treatment, the team checks what the patient can and cannot do yet so they can build a personalized recovery plan.

question: Which medication do nurses rely on to manage severe pre-eclampsia and stop dangerous seizures?

options.A: Oxytocin infusion
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Ferric folate syrup
options.D: Amoxicillin capsules

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is your go-to lifesaver drug for preventing and controlling eclamptic fits when blood pressure gets dangerously high.

question: Why is colchicine sometimes given along with NSAIDs to treat pericarditis?

options.A: To dissolve existing blood clots inside the heart chambers
options.B: To destroy resistant bacterial strains in the bloodstream
options.C: To permanently lower the patient's resting heart rate
options.D: To help prevent future episodes of the condition from returning

explanation: Colchicine is a helpful anti-inflammatory medicine added to treatment to stop pericarditis from coming back to trouble the patient again.

question: A woman carrying twins at 38 weeks asks to have her babies at home. What should you tell her?

options.A: Suggest waiting until labor is well established before deciding
options.B: Explain that multiple pregnancies require hospital care due to higher risks
options.C: Encourage home birth because twins are common in the community
options.D: Agree to attend the home birth if contractions are mild and regular

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Twin pregnancies carry higher chances of tricky presentations or heavy bleeding, so they truly need the safety of a health facility.

question: Which condition is a major safety risk specifically related to maternity care?

options.A: Obstructive sleep apnea
options.B: Chronic knee osteoarthritis
options.C: Diabetic foot ulceration
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Excessive bleeding after childbirth is one of the leading preventable causes of maternal mortality worldwide, requiring strict monitoring and rapid response. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the main job of the epiglottis when you swallow food?

options.A: To produce sound through the vocal cords
options.B: To filter dust particles out of the nose
options.C: To warm and humidify incoming air
options.D: To cover the windpipe and prevent food from entering the lungs

explanation: Think of the epiglottis as a tiny trapdoor. When you swallow, it folds down over your windpipe so your food and drink safely slide down the esophagus instead of going into your lungs!

question: What is obstetric fistula?

options.A: The premature closing of the birth canal due to hormonal imbalances
options.B: A sudden infection of the outer reproductive organs during early pregnancy
options.C: An abnormal opening between the vagina and bladder or rectum caused by prolonged labor
options.D: A complete failure of the ovaries to release eggs during the menstrual cycle

explanation: Well done! When labor is blocked in a narrow pelvis, the crushed tissue dies, leaving a hole (fistula) that causes leaking of urine or stool. It's a devastating condition we work hard to prevent.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to know the basic anatomy of these internal organs?

options.A: To properly assess pelvic pain and provide education
options.B: To diagnose complex endocrine disorders independently
options.C: To surgically repair damaged uterine tissue
options.D: To perform routine blood pressure checks

explanation: Understanding where organs sit helps nurses interpret patient symptoms and teach them about reproductive health. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why is a smaller bump size (5 mm) counted as positive for patients living with HIV?

options.A: They are more likely to have allergic reactions to the PPD liquid
options.B: They process the antigen much faster than healthy people
options.C: Their weakened immune systems cannot produce large inflammatory lumps
options.D: Their skin is thinner and harder to measure accurately

explanation: Because their immune systems are fighting harder battles, they can't throw a massive inflammatory response. So, even a smaller firm bump is a big red flag we take seriously! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h6)
